quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing footprint disclosed at the summit: Coherent has 'over 50 sites worldwide, but more than 20 are in the U.S.', a diversified global footprint, with Saxonburg, Pennsylvania - where the company was founded as a manufacturing company - still the global headquarters.
quarterly_data.figure: over 50 sites worldwide, but more than 20 are in the U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: Multi-Rail optical transport platform: scale-across customers are asking for a multifold increase in capacity, but the amplifier/fiber huts between data centers cannot grow - with today's technology a 4x capacity increase needs 4 times more space and 4 times more power, and in many of those roadside enclosures the power simply is not available. Multi-Rail lets Coherent 'increase capacity by a factor of four' within the same volumetric envelope, with power scaling sublinearly. Parthasarathi reported 'a lot of excitement from our hyperscale customers and our OEM customers.'
quarterly_data.figure: increase capacity by a factor of four

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-across demand driver: because data centers are power constrained, large AI workloads 'are being forced to be spread across multiple data centers because there’s just not enough power in one data center to process these large workloads', which drives demand for very high bandwidth connections between data centers. Parthasarathi split that opportunity into two functional blocks Coherent serves - data center interconnect (DCI) transceivers at the edge of the data center, and optical transport equipment (amplification, signal conditioning, fiber and signal health monitoring) sitting between the data centers - with bandwidth first and energy efficiency second as the metrics customers buy on.
